Title: If Mata Hari has a capacity of 10, can she effectively Call the Great Beast?

Messages.Author: david.cor...@gmail.com
Messages.Body:
Say you skill up Mata Hari to be a 10 cap and then play Call the Great
Beast ---

Does the card text trigger as the action succeeds?

Does the Great Beast come into play?

Is Mata Hari burned as a Baali?

david.cor...@gmail.com wrote:
> Say you skill up Mata Hari to be a 10 cap and then play Call the Great
> Beast ---

Let's assume you mean "to be an 11 cap"...

> Does the card text trigger as the action succeeds?

I would imagine, while she is playing the card, the following happens:
1. This card is placed on her (the acting Baali).
2. Eleven ritual counters are placed on it.

Then, while the card is in play:
1. If Mata is a Baali, she may place a counter on it a +1 stealth
action.
2. If this card has more than 10 counters, Mata is burned if she is a
Baali and you choose three disciplines etc.

Since it reads "and", both things happen, like when using Temptation on
an untapped vampire. Neither is required for the other to happen, so
when you have 11 counters, you should not burn her unless she is a
Baali, and you should get a Great Beast.

> Does the Great Beast come into play?

I would say it does, yes.

> Is Mata Hari burned as a Baali?

Only if she is a Baali.

Cool trick, man, hope LSJ confirms.

-- Brian

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <1132816039....@g47g2000cwa.googlegroups.com>,

firstco...@aol.com writes:
>Since the card "Call the Great Beast" has text that puts it in play,
>and that text is on the card before the "burn this card when it has
>more than 10 counters" text, doesn't that mean that CtGB is put into
>play before the "burn this Baali" effect would happen?

It does, but it's put there as part of action resolution and so - for
the purposes of the card - she's still a Baali at that point.

The card text then notices it has 11 counters, during action resolution.

Consider: Waters of Duat is put into play by Mata Hari. There are
definitions of what the vampire is, later on the card: not unique, must
hunt this turn and same sect as the acting Follower of Set. Mata Hari
would trigger as the acting Follower of Set.

Hence, we can see that even after a card is put in play, it can trigger
during the action. Call the Great Beast appears to do this too: Call
the Great Beast is put in play with counters. There is a condition
about what the counters do. It's triggered.

--
James Coupe

First, I want to make sure that I'm correct when I say that counters
can only be on a card while it is in play.

Assuming that's correct, which seems safe to assume, then the card must
already be in play to have counters, and must have counters to be
burned, and therefore must be in play to be burned.

If you're suggesting that CtGB's text has two functions:
1) while you're playing this card, if there are 11 counters, burn this
Baali, and
2) while this card is in play, if there are 11 counters, burn this
Baali,

then how many other cards' texts can be applied once while being played
and once while in play? The only other card I can think of right now
which has text which could be read to have effect while being played OR
while in play, is repulsion. From a previous thread, on Repulsion:

"Repulsion OBE puts a card into play. The card, being in play, grants
additional stealth."

That is, you don't play Repulsion to get stealth: You play repulsion.
Then, when it's in play, you have stealth.

If its text applies while being played AND when in play, then you would
have 1 stealth from playing it--much as CtGB's text applies while being
played--and 1 stealth from it being in play. Does this seem relevant?

More after you post, I suppose. I'll wait for you to
correct/agree/clarify and then go from there.

-- Brian

> If CtGB is in play, and the effect to burn the Baali comes from CtGB,
> then the "burn this Baali" effect is an effect from a card in play.

That logic would mean that adding 11 counter is an effect from the card
in play. It is not. It is from the card being played. It could easily
have been ruled to be from the card in play. That ambiguity is what
is resolved by the current ruling.

Just because the play of a card also puts that card in play doesn't
mean that every effect generated by the play is to be considered to
have come from the card in play instead.

See Create Gargoyle, for example. If Mata Hari plays it as a Tremere,
then the Gargoyle (a card in play) is a Tremere Slave, not a Ravnos
Slave. The enslavement is set by the play of the card, not by the
card in play.

> If "burn this Baali" is an effect from a card in play, and Mata Hari's
> ability does not consider her to be a Baali for effects from cards in
> play, then Mata Hari is not burned from this effect.

True, but the "if" premise is not true.
The "burn this Baali" comes from the play of the card when it is played
by an 11-cap vampire.

> How could it be understood to be otherwise--are you saying that the
> effect to burn the Baali also comes from the resolution of the action?

Yes, if the acting vampire's capacity is 11.

Hmm, this ruling makes Rötschreck peculiar when countered by Psyche!,
or Telepathic Tracking.

You're saying that the effects from Call the Great Beast are not
ordered, or at least that the order is NOT: Put this card on the minion
and add counters -> Give this minion an ability -> Control the number of
counters and invoke effect.

I read the text as when the action has fully resolved the card is placed
on the minion and counters are added to the card. After resolution the
minion with the card has an ability and it's time to check the number
of counters in order to eventually invoke an effect.

Compare:

Rötschreck: Put this card on the minion -> End combat -> Invoke effect
-> Add primary persistent effect -> Add secondary persistent effect.

In the latter card there's a ruling that allows for an insertion in the
chain of effect. Chain is broken after "End combat", ie, there's a
distinct order of events.

For me this is a matter of timing, the way that a cap 2 inf for vampire
equipping with Drum of Xipe Totec is NOT allowed to Forced March the
action because CEL is not gained until AFTER the action is resolved.

On a side-note. I guess that Rötschreck actually stays on the receiving
minion until the controller of Rötschreck is ousted, the controller of
the minion is ousted or game ends. Not that it matters much apart from
decks able to manipulate ashheaps.

If I've misunderstood things completely, please reply with an exstended
answer :)

Sten During

Compare instead Corruption.
After placing counters, a change-of-control effect is produced if the
weight is right. This change of control is produced by the play of
the Corruption card.

> Rötschreck: Put this card on the minion -> End combat -> Invoke effect
> -> Add primary persistent effect -> Add secondary persistent effect.
>
> In the latter card there's a ruling that allows for an insertion in the
> chain of effect. Chain is broken after "End combat", ie, there's a
> distinct order of events.

Not entirely correct.
There is no "primary"/"secondary" distinction.

An effect which ends combat and does something else as part of
its (singular) resolution can be disrupted as combat ends, since
ending combat invariably produces an "as combat is ending" effect.

Messages.Author: LSJ

Sten During wrote:
> Primary and secondary persistent effects are "doesn't untap as
> normal" and "burn this card". As per earlier rulings the untapping
> of cards goes before any other "during untap phase", so the
> doesn't untap as normal occurs before the burn clause.

Actually, it's a negative -- the absence of activity, so it doesn't go
in any order.

If you have an effect that says you cannot gain pool for the Edge
during your untap phase, do you order that effect before or after
you gain pool for the Edge? No, it just is. It's "always on",
preventing some other effect from being applied.

> BTW, DOES the vampire keep the Rötschreck indefinitely if Pshyche!
> has been played?

No. The card in play makes a "burn me" effect (at the appropriate
time).
